# Configuration

<!-- Generated from crates/vtium-settings/src/keys.rs; do not edit. `VTIUM_BLESS=1 cargo test -p vtium generated_files` rewrites it. -->

vtium reads one file, `vtium.conf` in the configuration directory (`--configdir`, `/etc/vtium` by default), then its command line, which wins over the file (ADR-1403 D2). vtium never reads `/etc/kmscon` or a seat file such as `seat0.seat.conf`: a `kmscon.conf` from kmscon is copied to `/etc/vtium/vtium.conf` by hand, and vtium reads the keys `kmscon` takes, in the ways the vtium crate's README, "Reading the configuration", sets out. With no file, vtium runs its defaults and its compiled-in heads and rules. The file is read once, at start: a change applies when vtium starts again, as at a restart of its service.

The file has two parts (ADR-1403 D3). Every line above the first section heading is the top level: vtium's own keys, the defaults every head inherits, and the flow's `version` and `policy`. From the first section heading on come the sections: a `[look NAME]` for each look, which names a frit and its size, a `[head NAME]` for each head, and one `[rules]` list, which sends each display and each input device to a head (ADR-1401 D3). A file with a section needs `version = 1`. A head's section wins over its look's, and its look's over the top level, for the keys the table below says each may set (ADR-1403 D5).

vtium reads vtium.conf only when root owns it, or, for a vtium that runs as another user, that user, and neither its group nor others can write it or a directory above it. It reads none of a file that fails, runs its compiled-in configuration, and says which path fails and the command that mends it, `chown root:root PATH` or `chmod go-w PATH`.

`vtium check-config [--no-devices] [FILE]` reads vtium.conf, or FILE in its place to check it before it is installed, both its parts in one run, as the start would, through the start's parser and evaluator (ADR-1401 D7). It applies nothing, exits 1 on any warning of the keys and on each error and warning of the sections, each named with its line, and on a file whose flow wires no complete route: a display present that its first matching rule sends to a head that a keyboard present reaches (ADR-1403 D3). With no display or no keyboard present, or with `--no-devices`, it judges the rules alone and says so. It notes on standard output what it does not count: the density points convert at, and of the sections each rule sending input to a head by `id` or `name` alone, where no udev daemon runs, each rule using a key that reads udev's database, each rule using `connector-path:`, which it cannot check against the displays present since it opens no card to read a connector's `PATH`, a head no rule names, every head isolated, and what the devices present find: each rule matching none of them, each device no rule places with what the policy gives it, no head that can be the active head having a display, under a closed policy no keyboard reaching any head, a head claiming pointers while every keyboard is claimed elsewhere, every keyboard ignored, and a head whose only keyboard is one device (ADR-1401 D9). It reads the devices from sysfs and udev's database, `/run/udev/data`, and opens nothing under `/dev`. A FILE that root does not own, or that others can write, is checked all the same, with a note, since installing it makes it root's.

A top-level line holds one key: `key=value`, or a switch's `key` to turn it on and `no-key` to turn it off. A section's line is `key = value`. `#` starts a comment at the start of a line or after a blank; a `#` inside a word, or one that opens a `#rrggbb` value, is part of the value, and `\#` after a blank is a literal `#`. Spaces and tabs around the key and the value are dropped. On the command line a key is `--key=VALUE` or `--key VALUE`, and a switch `--key` or `--no-key`.

vtium reports, once at start, a top-level key it does not know, however often it appears, and a value it cannot use: a number out of bounds, which it clamps, and a value it cannot read, which it ignores, keeping the value the sources before it gave. An error in a section drops what ADR-1401 D7 says it takes, and never a top-level key. It reads at most 65536 bytes of the file and 8192 of a line.

`install/vtium.conf.example` in `crates/vtium` lists the same keys at their defaults, under the same sections, then the compiled-in looks, heads and rules. Source cites the specification or the decision a key comes from.

## Session and terminal

The command each console runs, the terminal type it sees, and how much of its output vtium keeps.

| Key | Option | Type | Default | Bound | Read by | Set in | What | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `login` | `--login -- COMMAND...`, `-l` | command | unset | 4095 bytes in a file | vtium | top level, `[head NAME]`, command line | The command each console runs, such as a login prompt or a shell. When unset, the command is `/bin/login -p` with `reset-env` on and `/bin/login` with it off. ## Displays

Each display's resolution, colors and density, how long vtium waits for a display when it starts, and how it draws to them.

| Key | Option | Type | Default | Bound | Read by | Set in | What | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `use-original-mode` | `--use-original-mode`, `--no-use-original-mode` | switch | off | on or off | vtium-platform | top level, command line | Keep each display's current resolution. When off, vtium sets each display's preferred resolution. | src/config.c:1416; vtium/vtium#5 |
| `mode` | `--mode=VALUE` | resolution, one per line | unset | names of 63 bytes, each side 1 to 65535 | vtium-platform | top level, command line | A display's resolution and refresh rate. `WxH[@RATE]` sets it for every display, `[CONNECTOR]WxH` for one connector, and `GPU[CONNECTOR]WxH` for one connector on one graphics card, named by its udev `ID_PATH`. Write one `mode` line per display; the most specific match wins. When unset, each display uses its preferred resolution. Setting it turns `use-original-mode` off. | src/config.c:546-660, 1417, 1541-1548 |
| `display-depth` | `--display-depth=VALUE` | one of `auto`, `1`, `gray4`, `gray16`, `color` | `auto` | the choices | vtium-render | top level, `[look NAME]`, command line | How many colors or shades each display can show. `1` is black and white: each character cell is lit or dark by its colors, never by their brightness. `gray4` and `gray16` are for gray panels of 4 or 16 shades; vtium sends color and the panel converts it. `color` is full color. `auto` uses what the display reports: 1 bit for an fbdev device that says so, or the levels of a known DRM panel driver. | the operator on vtium/vtium#135 |
| `display-dpi` | `--display-dpi=VALUE` | number (dpi) | unset | 20 to 1000, clamped | vtium | top level, `[look NAME]`, command line | The pixel density (DPI) used to turn `font-size` and a font set's `size=` from points into pixels, instead of the density each display reports. When unset, vtium measures each display's density from the physical size it reports. If a display reports none, vtium assumes 96 DPI and logs a warning once for that display. | the operator on vtium/vtium#145 |
| `display-wait` | `--display-wait=VALUE` | number (s), or `forever` | 10 | 0 to 600, clamped, or `forever` | vtium | top level, command line | How long vtium waits for a display when it starts, counted from when its VT is shown. If no display appears in that time, vtium exits with status 1, so the unit's `OnFailure=` can start a getty. When vtium.conf's policy is closed, vtium waits as long as it takes, as with `forever`. vtium counts only while the VT is its own. If another program takes the VT before vtium's first frame is on screen, as X does at boot when it starts on another VT, vtium waits for the VT to come back and then starts the full wait again. With 0, vtium does not wait: only a display that is ready when the VT is shown counts. `forever` waits as long as it takes, for a machine whose only display is a USB adapter (DisplayLink, `udl`) that may be plugged in at any time. Once a display has appeared, vtium never exits for lack of one. | the operator on vtium/vtium#21 and #270 |
| `display-buffers` | `--display-buffers=VALUE` | one of `1`, `2`, `3` | unset | the choices | vtium-platform | top level, command line | How many frame buffers each display keeps (DRM displays only; every display gets the same number). `3` is triple buffering: no frame waits for the previous one to reach the screen, at the cost of one more frame of memory per display (8 MB at 1080p). `2` is double buffering. `1` is single buffering, which uses the least memory, but vtium then draws into the buffer on screen, so a half-drawn frame can show. A framebuffer device (fbdev) always keeps one buffer. When unset, the build decides: the number it was built with (`VTIUM_DISPLAY_BUFFERS`), or else 3 in a build with optional features, 2 in the smallest build (minspec), and 1 only in a build smaller than that. `vtium config get display-buffers` prints the draft's value followed by `draft`, or the build's default followed by `default` (`unset` when the build sets no number, in which case the rule above decides). | ADR-1401 D2; the C reference's drm2d kept 2, src/video/drm2d_internal.h:49 |
| `hwaccel` | `--hwaccel`, `--no-hwaccel` | switch | off | on or off | vtium | top level, command line | Draw with the GPU, in a build that supports it. It is off unless vtium was built with it on (`VTIUM_HWACCEL`). `vtium config get hwaccel` prints the draft's value followed by `draft`, or the build's default followed by `default`. `vtium config set hwaccel on` turns it on in the draft. | src/config.c:1413 |
| `render-timer` | `--render-timer=VALUE` | one of `none`, `osd`, `log`, `both` | `none` | the choices | vtium-render | top level, command line | Measure each display's frame times once a second, and write the figures to the log, show them on screen, or both. | src/config.c:972-1015, 1475 |

| `private-color-registers` | `--private-color-registers`, `--no-private-color-registers` | switch | on | on or off | vtium-term | top level, command line | Give each sixel image its own colors (mode 1070, after a reset).
